prose:ch07-objectives:
Chapter objectives. This chapter will help readers to:

  • Describe the core functions that any health workforce registry should provide.
  • Distinguish minimum functions from optional or advanced ones.
  • Provide a requirements catalogue that countries can adapt for specification and procurement.
prose:ch07-key-messages:
Key messages

  • The core is small: identify each worker uniquely, hold a trusted record, keep it current, and answer queries.
  • Functions can be delivered by one system or shared across several connected systems.
  • Non-functional requirements (security, availability, offline use, languages) matter as much as functions.
  • Requirements should be written so that they can be tested.

dt:hrh-dt-01-registration-eligibility:
Decision-table. Health worker registration eligibility and identifier assignment (HRH-DT-01)

Purpose. This table decides what happens to a registration application: register and license, hold it for duplicate review or pending verification, or reject it. The registration officer at the regulatory body uses it when processing a new application (processes HRH-BP-01 and HRH-BP-02). It serves the identity and records requirements Assign a unique, persistent health worker identifier, Search, match and merge duplicate records across source systems, Create, view, update and archive the health worker record… and Hold supporting evidence, such as certificates.

Decision table HRH-DT-01 (the first matching rule applies) formalizes the rules in Section 7.1 (Identity management) and Section 7.2 (Records) governing when a registration application creates a new persistent health worker identifier (Assign a unique, persistent health worker identifier), reuses an existing identifier across cadres or specialties, holds a candidate duplicate for manual adjudication (Search, match and merge duplicate records across source systems), or rejects an application lacking primary-source qualification attestation (Create, view, update and archive the health worker record…, Hold supporting evidence, such as certificates).

Source passages cited: Identity management, Assign a unique, persistent health worker identifier, Search, match and merge duplicate records across source systems, Create, view, update and archive the health worker record…, Hold supporting evidence, such as certificates, and Register and license a new graduate. Qualitative states come strictly from the source text; no numeric matching scores or day thresholds are invented.

dt:hrh-dt-02-lifecycle-status-transition:
Decision-table. Health worker lifecycle and licence status transition (HRH-DT-02)

Purpose. This table decides a practitioner's new registration and licence status after a lifecycle event (renewal, expiry, suspension, revocation, reinstatement, employment update, retirement, emigration or death), always keeping the earlier states. The registration officer uses it when recording such an event (processes HRH-BP-01 and HRH-BP-03). It serves the lifecycle requirements Manage status changes and Support renewals, recording of continuing professional development.

Decision table HRH-DT-02 (the first matching rule applies) formalizes the rules in Section 7.3 (Lifecycle management) and Section 4.3 (Health worker lifecycle) for transitioning a practitioner's registration and licence status across renewal, employment updates, suspension, revocation, reinstatement, retirement/emigration and death (Manage status changes), while preserving all historical states without overwriting prior records (Support renewals, recording of continuing professional development).

Source passages cited: Lifecycle management, Manage status changes, Support renewals, recording of continuing professional development, Renew a licence, Update employment or place of practice, and Health worker lifecycle. Only qualitative states named in the text are used; country-specific renewal intervals or CPD point thresholds are not hardcoded.

dt:hrh-dt-03-verification-and-access-res:
Decision-table. Verification service and tiered disclosure response (HRH-DT-03)

Purpose. This table decides how much of a health worker's record to disclose when someone asks for it: public status only, an operational view for authorized employers and clinical systems, de-identified aggregates for planners, the full record for the health worker or the custodian, or nothing. The registration officer and the registry apply it to verification and data requests (processes HRH-BP-03 and HRH-BP-05), under the disclosure policy the governance body approves (HRH-BP-06). It serves the verification, analytics and access requirements Confirm registration and licence status in real time for…, Issue digital, verifiable credentials or certificates (for example a…, Respond to verification requests from other countries, Data quality reports for registry managers, Record the source and date of each data item and Security.

Decision table HRH-DT-03 (the first matching rule applies) formalizes the rules in Section 7.4 (Verification services), Section 7.5 (Analytics), Section 6.2 (Legal foundations) and Section 6.3 (Data stewardship) for tiered disclosure when responding to status verification and data access requests across public lookup (Confirm registration and licence status in real time for…), system-to-system clinical/HR verification (Issue digital, verifiable credentials or certificates (for example a…), online/offline verifiable credentials (Respond to verification requests from other countries), de-identified analytics extracts (Data quality reports for registry managers), and self/stewardship record inspection (Record the source and date of each data item, Security).

prose:ch07-nfr-intro: Non-functional requirements matter as much as functions. The initial set, from the chapter's key messages:
nfreq:NFR-01:
Non-functional-requirement. Security

NFR-01 Security. Health workers' personal data are protected in storage and in transit, with role-based access for people and authenticated access for systems (see Chapter 12).
nfreq:NFR-02:
Non-functional-requirement. Availability

NFR-02 Availability. Verification services are available when employers, the public and other systems need them, with agreed service levels.
nfreq:NFR-03:
Non-functional-requirement. Offline and low-connectivity use

NFR-03 Offline and low-connectivity use. Registration and verification work in low-connectivity settings, including through paper or assisted channels where needed.
nfreq:NFR-04:
Non-functional-requirement. Languages

NFR-04 Languages. The registry and its public views support the languages its users need.
nfreq:NFR-05:
Non-functional-requirement. Testable requirements

NFR-05 Testable requirements. Every requirement is written so that conformance to it can be tested.

prose:ch08-objectives:
Chapter objectives. This chapter will help readers to:

  • Explain the main architecture options for a registry in non-technical terms.
  • Help countries choose a pattern that fits their governance, existing systems and capacity.
  • Set out principles that keep the registry scalable, reusable and independent of any one product.
